missingEvidence: Liquidation composition is established; advantage over standard liquidation tooling is not established.
Current oracle address is read, but feed freshness/deviation and full risk state are unverified.
Historical exchange rates, full funding attribution, helper control and all costs remain incomplete.
No currently eligible borrower/executable opportunity established.
nextChecks: Match every debt repayment and collateral redemption to token/native flows in raw receipts.
Identify all pool/token contracts and actual withdrawal beneficiaries.
Aggregate successful and failed execution costs and funding costs over the same window.
If complete accounting is non-positive or unavailable liquidity blocks redemption, reject the opportunity.
alternativeExplanations: This is standard liquidation tooling rather than a distinct edge.
A helper may use pre-existing inventory or third-party funding.
Retained tokens, capital costs and failed attempts can offset the visible inflow.

missingEvidence: Historical positive token flow is not full-window net profit.
Current quotes are views, not an executable swap simulation.
Caller and sponsor resources, allowances, competition and full cost must be rechecked before any opportunity claim.
Source/bytecode equivalence, token behavior and historical upgrades not independently proved.
nextChecks: Reconcile actual input/output transfers with route calldata and historical pool reserves.
Calculate costs across all 245 attempts, not just the two successful samples.
Reconstruct execution at the historical block and test whether current reserves still support positive all-in economics.
Reject profitability if all-in token-equivalent costs consume the observed difference.
alternativeExplanations: Visible token increase can be smaller than total resource and failed-transaction costs.
A sampled route may be a one-off price imbalance with limited capacity.
Token/pool accounting or subsidies may explain the flows; deployment identities need further verification.
